works.author: Oecumenius of Tricca
works.authorNote: 10th-century Byzantine bishop/compiler; PG 118-119 gathers the Greek catena tradition on Paul's Epistles (and, per the parent volume's own preface, possibly the Acts/Catholic-epistle catena too) under his name — attribution to a single 'Oecumenius' is itself debated in scholarship, but PG's ascription is what this citation follows.
works.title: Commentarius in Epistolam ad Philippenses
works.titleEn: Commentary on the Epistle to the Philippians
works.queueNote: PG paired-pilot P3 (pg-paired-pilot.md §7): the spec recommended the commentary on Jude (or 2-3 John) as the volume's smallest complete lemma-and-gloss unit, on the assumption Catholic-epistle commentary is in PG 118. It is NOT: the local Calfa harvest of PG118_text.txt (37,508 lines) runs Romans through Philippians only (ends mid-volume with the doxology 'Τέλος σὺν Θεῷ τῆς πρὸς Φιλιππησίους'); Jude/2-3 John and the rest of the Pauline corpus (Colossians onward) are apparently in PG 119 or simply outside this Calfa clone's scope — not investigated further, per rule 8 (don't hunt past what's in hand). Philippians (14,089 Greek words, Calfa pp. 641-674) is the smallest complete epistle-commentary actually present in the file, smaller than Galatians (15,862w) and Ephesians (18,927w), the file's other short candidates. It is lemma-and-gloss throughout (scriptural lemma in quotation marks, then gloss — e.g. opens '«Τοῖς ἁγίοις ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.» Ἦσαν γὰρ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι...'), satisfying the genre purpose of P3 even though the specific book differs from the recommendation. NOTE: translationStatus deliberately absent (no verified none-status is in hand for this specific work; the deploy badge fails safe to 'New English translation' per CLAUDE.md rule 8 — do not hunt to fill this in).

works.queueNote: Sermon I of Isidore Glabas's Sermones IV in B. Mariam Virginem (see parent entry `isidore-glabas-sermones`, PG 139, 11-164, four sermons: Nativity/Entry/Annunciation/Dormition) — this is the Nativity sermon, split out as PG paired-pilot P2 (pg-paired-pilot.md §7). Span determined at harvest 2026-07-31: Calfa page 13 opens ΑΟΓΟΣ Αʹ (Ἐις τὴν γέννησιν...); the sermon's closing doxology (Ἀμήν) falls partway through Calfa page 27, immediately followed by ΑΟΓΟΣ Βʹ (Sermon II, on the Entry) in the same page/column. The chunker truncates page 27 at that Ἀμήν via a calfa-patches entry so Sermon II's opening text is never pulled into this work. KNOWN SCAN GAP (found at harvest): 3 of this sermon's 15 Calfa pages have NO corresponding leaf in raw/scans/pg139/patrologiaecurs63migngoog_djvu.xml — pages 13-14 (cols 11-14, the sermon's opening) and page 21 (cols 27-28, mid-sermon) match no scan leaf above noise level (best hit ≤3 tokens across all 788 leaves, vs 11-31 hits on every neighboring page). Leaves 0-7 of this scan are Google/PG-series front matter, not this column range — those two Calfa pages simply have no leaf in this copy. Latin twin is UNAVAILABLE for those 3 pages; the Latin twin chunks that span them are correspondingly under-length (see src/pg-latin/isidore-glabas-sermo-1/manifest.json). GAP CLOSED 2026-07-31 (coordinator follow-up): patrologicursus73migngoog.pdf (702pp, a second archive.org item / different physical-copy scan) DOES carry all three missing columns intact at PDF pages 10 (cols 11-12), 11 (cols 13-14), and 18 (cols 27-28) -- confirmed by direct page inspection plus tesseract grc+lat OCR, >=2 distinctive Greek tokens per page (4, 4, 3 hits). That PDF has no embedded text layer of its own, so the Latin was extracted via tesseract 300dpi render+OCR (render+read fallback) rather than a djvu.xml crop -- see data/pg-latin-altsource/isidore-glabas-sermo-1.json for the per-page text and provenance, each explicitly marked as coming from a DIFFERENT witness than the rest of the twin. The archive.org patrologia-volumes/139_text.pdf (text-layer variant) was also checked and confirmed to be the SAME physical scan as the primary (identical page content, same gap) -- no help there.

Mariam Virginem (parent `isidore-glabas-sermones`, PG 139, 11-164) -- the Entry sermon, split out per pg-paired-pilot.md §8a.C as the first queue addition after the PG gate opened. Span from the Calfa headings: ΛΟΓΟΣ Βʹ opens partway through page 27 (the same page/column where Sermon I ends) and ΛΟΓΟΣ Γʹ opens 55 chars into page 43, so both ends are truncated by data/calfa-patches/isidore-glabas-sermo-2.json. FULL SCAN-LEAF COVERAGE -- unlike Sermon I, every one of these 17 Calfa pages has a leaf in patrologiaecurs63migngoog (pages 28-30 are parity-filled, not leaf-gaps), so the Latin twin and the third-witness Greek are available across the whole sermon. NOTE a genuine side-parity flip inside the span: page 42 carries greekCol 69 (odd side) but page 43 carries 72 (even side); both are token-verified, so the chunker's per-page greekCol is trusted over the parity rule there. The Marian epithet table built for Sermon I governs this work (translation-style.md, Register PG/Greek, high rhetorical homily) -- it was written to govern the set. NOT YET TRANSLATED: harvest + gate done, translation launch still needs its own hard stop.
works.statusProvenance: translationStatus 'none' is INHERITED FROM THE SET, not verified for this sermon alone: the 2026-07-03 triage checked Isidore Glabas's Sermones IV as a unit (parent `isidore-glabas-sermones` — not in Daley or Cunningham, the two anthologies that would carry them), and sermo-1 rests on exactly the same evidence. Recorded explicitly rather than left to look like a per-work verification, per CLAUDE.md rule 8: the badge is the one claim on the site a reader cannot check, so where its evidence came from must be legible. If that set-level check is ever doubted, it is doubted for all four sermons at once.

works.ladderCaveat: Migne's editor in this volume states 'hanc narrationem mire corruptam saepe divinando Latine reddidimus' (foot of col 1421/1422). Where he divines, the Latin is NOT independent of the Greek. The whole-text hand-check against the plate is the load-bearing verification for this work, not the twin.
